risks.risk: Engines may be seized or have poor compression.
risks.proof: A video showing a technician rotating the crankshaft manually or a compression test gauge reading for each cylinder.

risks.risk: Internal sludge or heavy carbon buildup from poor maintenance.
risks.proof: Clear photos of the cylinder head through the oil filler cap or with the valve cover removed.
risks.if_unproven: as requiring a complete internal teardown and cleaning.

risks.proof: Close-up photos of the engine block identification stamps and serial numbers.
risks.if_unproven: at the value of the least expensive engine model mentioned.

risks.risk: Missing essential external components like sensors, manifolds, or wiring.
risks.proof: Individual 360-degree photos of each engine unit.
risks.if_unproven: as bare long blocks without accessories.

proof_requests: Close-up photos of the engine block stamps/ID tags for every unit to verify models.
Photos of the engines with oil caps removed to check for sludge.
A video of the crankshaft being turned on a sample of the units to ensure they are not seized.
A detailed inventory list matching the white marker notations on the blocks to specific models.
response.reason: While the witness confirms the presence of engines, they could not verify any specific brands or models. Since the value varies significantly between a Camry engine and a Lexus RX350 engine, identification is required before a price can be set.
